name: Epithelioid Hemangioma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No formal standardized criteria; diagnosis based on histopathology and clinical presentation

criteria.description: Presence of well-formed blood vessels lined by plump epithelioid endothelial cells with inflammatory infiltrate rich in eosinophils
Solitary or multiple erythematous to violaceous papules or nodules typically located on head and neck region
Endothelial cells positive for vascular markers such as CD31 and CD34

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of characteristic epithelioid endothelial cells with eosinophilic infiltrate plus compatible clinical presentation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Differentiation from epithelioid hemangioendothelioma and Kimura disease is critical

pathognomonic.symptomName: Erythematous to violaceous dermal papules or nodules
pathognomonic.notes: Typically located on head and neck

pathognomonic.symptomName: Histopathological presence of epithelioid endothelial cells with eosinophilic infiltrate
searchTerms: tumor with specific endothelial cells and eosinophils
histology showing epithelioid cells with eosinophilic infiltrate
pathology with endothelial cells and eosinophils

common.symptomName: Slow progressive growth of cutaneous lesions

occasional.symptomName: Occasional systemic symptoms such as low-grade fever
searchTerms: occasional low fever and systemic symptoms
intermittent mild fever with other symptoms

rare.symptomName: Involvement of deeper soft tissues or muscle
searchTerms: tumor invading deep soft tissues or muscle

imaging: Ultrasound may show well-circumscribed hypoechoic nodules
MRI can delineate lesion extent in deeper involvement
other: Histopathology showing epithelioid endothelial cells with eosinophilic infiltrate

distinguishingFeatures: Malignant vascular tumor with infiltrative growth
Histology shows less inflammatory infiltrate and more atypia
Often involves deeper tissues and viscera
Painless subcutaneous masses with prominent lymphoid follicles
Marked peripheral eosinophilia and elevated IgE
Histology shows lymphoid hyperplasia without epithelioid endothelial cells

redFlags: Involvement of deeper soft tissues or systemic symptoms
references: Wang J, et al. Epithelioid Hemangioma: Clinicopathologic and Immunohistochemical Study of 50 Cases. Am J Surg Pathol. 2019.
Fetsch JF, et al. Epithelioid Hemangioma (Angiolymphoid Hyperplasia with Eosinophilia): A Clinicopathologic Study of 116 Cases. Hum Pathol. 2004.
